about: Trainer: collision lab (Unit 4). Explore runs ApPhysMath.collisionLab.run, a closed-form model of two carts whose bumper is a spring that loads at stiffness k and unloads at k/e² (e = 0 Velcro, 1 elastic): momentum is conserved at every instant, the center of mass moves at constant velocity, and the impulse is the area under the force-time pulse. The validator regenerates 300 problems per context and type and recomputes every key from the problem's own numbers.
intro: Two carts on a low-friction track. Set their masses and velocities, choose a bumper from sticky Velcro to a bouncy spring, and crash them. The momentum bars and the center of mass show what is always conserved; the kinetic energy bars show what depends on the bumper; the force-time graph shows the impulse as an area. Explosion mode pushes two carts apart from rest.
howItWorks:
• Momentum p = mv, a vector: right is positive here. With no net external force on the two-cart system, the total momentum is constant, so the center of mass moves at a constant velocity vcm = p/M.
  • Kinetic energy K = ½mv² is conserved only in an elastic collision. In an inelastic one some becomes thermal energy and deformation; when the carts stick (perfectly inelastic) the most is lost.
  • Impulse J = Δp = the area under the force-time graph = FavgΔt. A stiffer bumper gives a shorter, taller spike with the same area.
  • Momentum or energy? Start a collision from momentum; use energy for motion with no collision (ramps, springs, friction).

The bumper is a spring that pushes back with F = kx; the motion is computed exactly, not sketched. On the exam you will not be asked for both final velocities of an elastic collision (that needs simultaneous equations); here the lab shows them so you can see the bars.
